response.rationale: R5 best captures the full syndrome: parous woman with contraceptive use, negative TB/infectious workup, outer-half tender swelling, fistula with orange-peel skin, and MRI showing multiple thick-walled enhancing lesions throughout the gland. R2 is the same entity but lacks the idiopathic/lobular specificity. R1 periductal mastitis is less consistent with the outer-half location, absence of nipple discharge, negative infectious workup, and diffuse glandular MRI pattern.

rejected.why: Periductal mastitis is typically periareolar/nipple-centered and often associated with nipple discharge or smoking; this case has an outer-half swelling, no nipple discharge, negative infectious workup, and diffuse glandular MRI lesions, making it less likely.
